book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 49 · Emergency Vehicle Operations
title: Safe Ambulance Operations: Check, Drive, Park, Land

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you've loaded, ridden in and maybe driven an ambulance. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Check the vehicle: the four Ss, and when it comes out of service
  2. Drive with due regard: lights and siren, intersections, backing up
  3. Park, load, and work safely with air ambulances

Textbook: Chapter 49, PDF pages 4119–4154
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, many of you have already loaded patients, ridden in the back, and maybe driven an ambulance. This chapter has no clinical protocol, but it covers one of the most dangerous parts of the job: if the ambulance doesn't arrive safely, nothing else you know can help the patient. As a PCP in the back, you decide how urgently the patient needs to travel, and many of your new interventions happen on the road. Today we'll cover three things: checking the vehicle, driving safely with or without lights and siren, and parking, loading, and working with air ambulances.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，很多人已经搬过病人上车、坐过后舱，也许还开过救护车。这一章没有临床流程，但讲的是这份工作最危险的部分之一：如果救护车不能安全到达，你会的一切都帮不了病人。作为在后舱负责的 PCP，由你决定病人需要多紧急的转运，而且你的很多新处置是在路上完成的。今天讲三件事：车辆检查；开不开警灯警笛都要安全驾驶；以及停车、装卸病人和配合空中救护。

slides.title: Check it before you drive it
slides.body:
Start→Steer→Stop→Stay running

Any threat to a four S = out of service now

  • Begin each shift with a walk-around: damage, leaks, lights, tires
  • Fuel first, then oil before starting the engine
  • Clean and restock after calls; check drug expiry dates
  • Date and sign the checklist: it's legal protection
slides.say: An ambulance must do four things one hundred percent of the time: start, steer, stop, and stay running. Any threat to one of these four Ss means the vehicle goes out of service immediately. Each shift starts with a walk-around: look for body damage, leaks, broken lights, and damaged tires. Then work through the checklist system by system: fuel first, then the oil, before you start the engine. Clean and restock after every call, and check medication expiry dates. Finally, date and sign the checklist; if there's ever a legal challenge, it protects you.
slides.sayZh: 救护车必须百分之百做到四件事：能启动、能转向、能停车、能持续运转。四个 S 中任何一个受到威胁，车辆就要立即停用。每个班次先绕车检查一圈：看车身损伤、漏液、灯不亮、轮胎损坏。然后按清单逐个系统检查：先查燃油，发动机启动前查机油。每次出车后清洁、补充物资，并检查药品有效期。最后在检查单上写日期并签名，万一遇到法律纠纷，它能保护你。

slides.title: Out of service, right now
slides.body:
FindingAction
Brake fade, even onceOut of service now
Brake pullOut of service now
Sewer smell (battery boiling)Out of service; hood closed; don't start
15 V or more, engine runningRegulator failed; replace now
Belt squealSignificant, but not immediate
slides.say: Some findings mean you stop using the ambulance right away. Brake fade is the feeling that the power brakes have disappeared, and even a single episode takes the vehicle out of service. Brake pull, where the wheel jerks to one side when you brake, also means out of service now. A sewer-gas smell can mean the battery is boiling, which also releases explosive hydrogen, so leave the hood closed and don't start the engine. With the engine running, the voltage should be thirteen point five to fourteen point five; fifteen or higher means the voltage regulator has failed. Belt squeal is important, but not an immediate out-of-service problem.
slides.sayZh: 有些发现意味着要马上停用救护车。刹车衰减是感觉刹车助力突然没了，哪怕只出现一次，车辆也要停用。刹车跑偏，就是一踩刹车方向盘被猛拽向一边，同样要立即停用。闻到下水道一样的臭味，可能是电池在沸腾，同时会产生易爆的氢气，所以不要打开引擎盖，也不要启动发动机。发动机运转时电压应在十三点五到十四点五伏之间，十五伏或以上说明调压器坏了。皮带异响很重要，但不属于必须立即停用的问题。

slides.q: Mid-shift, you brake and the pedal suddenly feels like it has lost its power assist. A minute later, the brakes feel normal. What should you do?
options: Keep driving and report it at the end of the shift
Take the ambulance out of service now
Drive non-emergency only until a mechanic checks it
Test the brakes a few more times and continue if they stay normal
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. Mid-shift, you brake and the pedal suddenly feels like it has lost its power assist. A minute later, the brakes feel normal again. What should you do? A, keep driving and report it at the end of the shift. B, take the ambulance out of service now. C, drive non-emergency only until a mechanic checks it. D, test the brakes a few more times and continue if they stay normal. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。班中你踩刹车时，踏板突然像失去了助力；一分钟后刹车又恢复正常。你该怎么做？A 继续开，下班时再报告；B 立即停用这辆救护车；C 在技师检查前只走非紧急模式；D 再多试几次刹车，正常就继续用。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. That was brake fade, and even a single episode takes the ambulance out of service immediately; stopping is one of the four Ss. A and C keep using a vehicle that may not stop when you need it to. D tests the brakes on the road, putting you, your partner, your patient, and the public at risk.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。这就是刹车衰减，哪怕只出现一次，救护车也要立即停用；能停车是四个 S 之一。A 和 C 都在继续使用一辆关键时刻可能停不下来的车。D 在路上测试刹车，会让你、搭档、病人和公众都陷入危险。

slides.title: Where crashes happen
slides.body:
• Top causes: wrong lane and too fast
  • Every intersection: expect traffic and other emergency vehicles
  • No escorts; if following, leave space, use a different siren
  • Tell families not to follow the ambulance
  • Avoid school zones at bell times, construction, rail crossings
  • Always brake in a straight line
slides.say: Most ambulance crashes come down to two things: being in the wrong lane and driving too fast. A worrying fact: nearly half of paramedics involved in a crash had another crash or a moving violation in the three years before. Approach every intersection carefully, and expect police or fire vehicles too. Don't follow a police car as an escort; drivers see the first vehicle and then pull out in front of you. If you must follow, leave plenty of space and use a different siren tone. Tell family members not to follow you. Plan routes that avoid school zones at bell times, construction, and railway crossings. And always brake in a straight line.
slides.sayZh: 大多数救护车事故归结为两点：车道不对，车速太快。一个令人担忧的事实：发生事故的急救员中，将近一半在之前三年里出过事故或有过交通违章。每个路口都要谨慎通过，还要预料到警车或消防车也可能出现。不要跟在警车后面当护航；其他司机只看到第一辆车，等它过去就会把车开到你前面。如果必须跟车，留出足够车距，并换一种不同的警笛音。告诉家属不要跟着救护车开。规划路线时，避开上下课时段的学校区域、施工区和铁路道口。还有，刹车一定要走直线。

slides.title: Lights and siren: a request
slides.body:
Lights and siren only ask for the right of way

  • Due regard: you still drive safely for everyone
  • Time saved: minimal. Crash risk: higher
  • Never for a non-emergent patient
  • The paramedic in the back decides, by patient stability
  • Not traffic, not the end of your shift
  • The type of call (kids, a colleague) must not change your driving
slides.say: Lights and siren don't give you the right of way; they only ask for it, and other drivers may not hear or understand. That's due regard: provincial law lets you use warning devices, but you must still drive safely for everyone. Studies show lights and siren save very little time, with a questionable effect on outcomes, and raise the risk of a crash. So never use them for a non-emergent patient. Who decides? The paramedic in the back with the patient, based on how stable the patient is, not on traffic or the end of your shift. And don't let an emotional call, like injured children or a colleague, speed you up.
slides.sayZh: 警灯警笛并不给你路权，只是请求路权，其他司机可能听不到，也可能不明白。这就是「应有注意」：省里的法律允许你使用警示装置，但你仍须顾及所有人的安全驾驶。研究显示，警灯警笛节省的时间很少，对预后的影响也存疑，却会增加撞车风险。所以非紧急病人绝不使用。谁来决定？是在后舱照护病人的急救员，依据是病人是否稳定，而不是路况或下班时间。也不要让情绪化的呼叫，比如受伤的孩子或同事，让你开得更快。

slides.title: Parking at the scene
slides.body:
SituationWhere to park
First on a highway sceneBetween traffic and the scene, as a buffer
Fire, leaking fuel or fumesAt least 30 m away, uphill and upwind
No hazardsAt least 15 m away
Scene already securedPast the wreckage, out of traffic
  • Night: hazard flashers may be safer; headlights off on two-lane roads
  • Always wear a reflective vest on the road
slides.say: Where you park can protect you or endanger you. If you're the first emergency vehicle at a highway crash, park between the oncoming traffic and the scene as a buffer. With fire, leaking fuel, or fumes, stay at least thirty metres away, uphill and upwind if you can; with no hazards, at least fifteen metres. If the scene is already secured, park past the wreckage, out of traffic. At night, roadside parking is especially dangerous: hazard flashers alone may be safer than all the overhead lights, and on a two-lane road, turn off your headlights so you don't blind oncoming drivers. Always wear a reflective vest.
slides.sayZh: 停车位置可以保护你，也可以害了你。如果你是第一辆到达高速事故现场的应急车辆，就停在来车方向和现场之间，充当缓冲。如果有火、漏油或有害气体，至少离开三十米，尽量在上坡和上风处；没有危险时至少十五米。如果现场已经控制，就停在事故点以远，避开车流。夜间在路边停车特别危险：只开危险警示灯可能比开全部顶灯更安全；在双车道上关掉前大灯，以免晃到对向司机。下车时一定穿反光背心。

slides.title: Backing up and loading
slides.body:
• Backing up = most common cause of damage. Plan to avoid it
  • Use a spotter; agree on signals, especially stop
  • Lose sight of the spotter? Stop. Window down
  • Everyone belted; patient with shoulder and lap straps
  • Children: a pediatric restraint, never an adult belt
  • Several patients: load the most serious last, unload first
slides.say: Backing up is the most common cause of ambulance damage, so plan your parking to avoid it. When you must back up, use a spotter. Talk first, agree on hand signals, especially the one for stop, and if you lose sight of the spotter, stop until you see them again. Keep your window down so you can hear warnings. Inside, everyone wears a seat belt, not just the patient, who is secured with shoulder and lap straps. Children need a proper pediatric restraint, never an adult belt, and shouldn't ride on the stretcher unless properly restrained. If you carry more than one patient, load the most serious last, so they come off first.
slides.sayZh: 倒车是救护车损坏最常见的原因，所以停车时就要尽量规划不用倒车。必须倒车时要有人指挥：先沟通，约定手势，尤其是「停」的手势；一旦看不见指挥员，就停车，等他回到视线内。车窗打开，才能听到警告。车内每个人都系安全带，不只是病人；病人用肩带和腰带固定。儿童要用合适的儿科约束装置，绝不能用成人安全带，没有妥善约束不能放在担架上转运。如果同车运送多名病人，最重的最后上车，这样到院时最先下车。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Daily vehicle check, dated and signed
  • Due regard; spotter when backing up
  • Everyone belted; equipment stowed
  • BC: start transport early; delegate egress prep
  • Attendant picks emergency mode by stability

PCP adds (BC, en route)

  • Hypovolemia: IV and bolus; reassess every 500 mL
  • Stroke: IV, 18 G above the wrist
  • Chest or abdominal trauma: IV, TXA if indicated

A smooth, safe drive is part of patient care.
slides.say: Every licence level does the daily vehicle check, drives with due regard, uses a spotter, makes sure everyone is belted, and keeps equipment stowed. Several BC protocols also tell all licence levels to start transport early and to delegate a crew member to prepare the exit. Whoever attends in the back chooses emergency mode based on the patient's stability. Now the PCP column: many PCP interventions are written to happen en route. In hypovolemia, you start the IV and give boluses on the way, reassessing every five hundred millilitres. In stroke and chest or abdominal trauma, the IV goes in en route too. So a smooth, safe drive is part of patient care.
slides.sayZh: 所有执照级别都要做每日车辆检查、以应有注意驾驶、倒车用指挥员、确保人人系安全带、设备收好固定。好几个 BC 流程还要求所有级别尽早开始转运，并指派一名队员提前准备撤离路线。无论谁在后舱负责，都按病人是否稳定来决定是否走紧急模式。再看 PCP 一栏：很多 PCP 处置在流程里就写明在途中进行。低血容量时，你在路上开静脉、补液，每五百毫升复评一次；卒中、胸部或腹部创伤时，静脉通路也是在途中建立。所以，平稳安全的驾驶本身就是病人照护的一部分。

slides.q: You're the PCP in the back with a stable patient: mild abdominal pain, normal vital signs. Your shift ends in 15 minutes and traffic is heavy. Your partner asks, "Lights and siren?" What's your answer?
options: Yes: heavy traffic justifies lights and siren
No: the patient is stable, so we drive with the normal flow of traffic
Yes, but only through the intersections
It's the driver's call, so let your partner decide
slides.say: Here's a decision for the attendant. You're the PCP in the back with a stable patient: mild abdominal pain and normal vital signs. Your shift ends in fifteen minutes, and traffic is heavy. Your partner asks, lights and siren? What's your answer? A, yes, heavy traffic justifies lights and siren. B, no, the patient is stable, so we drive with the normal flow of traffic. C, yes, but only through the intersections. D, it's the driver's call, so let your partner decide. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道后舱负责人的决策题。你是在后舱的 PCP，病人病情稳定：轻度腹痛，生命体征正常。还有十五分钟下班，路上很堵。搭档问：开警灯警笛吗？你怎么回答？A 开，路这么堵就该开；B 不开，病人稳定，我们随正常车流行驶；C 开，但只在过路口时开；D 这是司机的事，让搭档决定。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The attendant in the back decides, based on the patient's stability, not traffic or the end of the shift. Lights and siren save little time, raise the crash risk, and should never be used for a non-emergent patient. A and C make traffic the reason. D is wrong because the book gives this decision to the attendant, though the driver always stays responsible for due regard.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。由后舱负责人决定，依据是病人是否稳定，而不是路况或下班时间。警灯警笛省时很少、增加撞车风险，非紧急病人绝不应使用。A 和 C 都把路况当成理由。D 错在书里把这个决定交给后舱负责人，不过司机始终要对应有注意负责。

slides.title: Air ambulance: worth it?
slides.body:
• Helicopter: short trips to a trauma centre. Plane: long distance
  • Two questions: worth the risk? truly faster?
  • Count every step: lift-off, flight, landing, handover, packaging
  • Can help: remote areas, long extrication, severe traffic
  • Arrest or near-arrest: not a helicopter case
  • Decide early; the pilot decides whether to land
slides.say: Helicopters fly short distances, often straight from the scene to a regional trauma centre; fixed-wing airplanes cover long distances. Air transport can bring a higher level of care and reach remote areas, but before you call, ask two questions: does the patient's condition justify the risk, and will it really be faster? Count every step: starting the aircraft, the flight, landing, handover, and packaging the patient. In a city it's hard to justify, unless traffic is severe or extrication is long. Patients in cardiac arrest, or about to arrest, go by ground, because there's little room to work in a helicopter. Decide early, and remember: the pilot decides whether to land.
slides.sayZh: 直升机飞短途，常从现场直飞区域创伤中心；固定翼飞机负责长距离转运。空中救护能带来更高级别的救治、到达偏远地区，但呼叫之前先问两个问题：病情值得冒这个险吗？真的会更快吗？每一步都要算进去：飞机启动、飞行、降落、交接、包装病人。在城市里很难证明需要，除非交通严重拥堵或破拆时间很长。心脏骤停或即将骤停的病人走地面，因为直升机里几乎没有抢救空间。要尽早决定；也要记住，降不降落由飞行员说了算。

slides.title: Landing zone and approach
slides.body:
• Landing zone 30 × 30 m, firm, flat, nothing loose
  • Night: a light at each corner; never shine lights at the aircraft
  • Watch for overhead wires; clear people and vehicles
  • Approach only when the pilot signals, from the front or side
  • Avoid the tail rotor; crouch; downhill side on a slope
  • Vehicles 30 m back; no smoking within 100 m
slides.say: If a helicopter is coming to you, set up a landing zone about thirty by thirty metres, firm and level, with nothing loose that the rotors could suck up: caps, scarves, IV poles, even the stretcher sheet. Watch for overhead wires the pilot may not see, and clear away people and vehicles. At night, mark each corner with a light, and never shine lights up at the aircraft. After it lands, wait for the pilot's signal. Ideally the rotors are stopped; if they're turning, the tail rotor is the most dangerous part. Approach from the front or sides, crouched, and from the downhill side on a slope. Keep vehicles thirty metres back, and no smoking within one hundred metres.
slides.sayZh: 如果直升机要来接病人，就布置一个大约三十乘三十米、坚实平整的降落区，清走所有可能被旋翼卷起的松散物：帽子、围巾、输液架，连担架上的床单也要撤掉。注意飞行员可能看不见的架空电线，清走无关人员和车辆。夜间在每个角各放一盏灯，绝不要把灯往上照向飞机。落地后，等飞行员示意再靠近，最好等旋翼停转；如果旋翼还在转，尾旋翼是最危险的部位。从前方或侧面、弯着腰接近；停在斜坡上时从下坡一侧接近。车辆停在三十米以外，一百米内禁止吸烟。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Lights and siren are a request, never a guarantee: due regard
  • As attendant: emergency mode = stability, not the clock
  • Working en route: stow gear; stay belted whenever you can
  • Helicopter coming? Ask early about board type and length limits
  • A traction splint may make the patient too long for the aircraft
  • Brake fade, even once: out of service
slides.say: Now the watch-outs. First, lights and siren are a request, never a guarantee; due regard always applies, and the driver answers for every move. Second, as the attendant, base emergency mode on the patient's stability, not on traffic or the clock. Third, your new en route skills need a safe cabin: stow equipment so nothing can fly, and stay belted whenever you can. Fourth, if a helicopter is coming, ask early how to package the patient. Some aircraft take only a certain board, and some limit how long the patient can be, so a traction splint may not fit. Fifth, a single episode of brake fade takes the unit out of service.
slides.sayZh: 下面是要注意的地方。第一，警灯警笛只是请求，从来不是保证；应有注意始终适用，司机要为每个动作负责。第二，作为后舱负责人，是否走紧急模式看病人是否稳定，而不是路况或时间。第三，你在途中的新技能需要一个安全的车厢：设备收好固定，免得飞起来伤人；只要条件允许，就系好安全带。第四，如果有直升机要来，尽早问清病人该怎么包装：有的飞机只能放特定的脊柱板，有的限制病人的长度，牵引夹板可能放不进去。第五，刹车衰减哪怕只出现一次，车辆也要停用。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
Book: arrest patients go by ground to the nearest hospital, not by helicopter. BC's CPR guidance adds:

  • CPR is more effective when you're stationary
  • Moving with CPR: children, hypothermia, trauma, treatable causes
  • Move early during CPR only if dangerous, or CPR can't be done well there
  • Continue to 30 min (no ROSC, no shocks) or 40 min (any ROSC or shock)
  • Consult medical oversight to stop the arrest on scene
slides.say: There's no BC driving protocol, but one BC rule touches transport directly. The book says a patient in cardiac arrest should go by ground to the nearest hospital rather than wait for a helicopter. BC's CPR guidance adds that CPR is more effective when you're not moving. Transport with ongoing CPR may happen for children, hypothermia, trauma, or treatable causes. Move a patient early during CPR only if the scene is dangerous, or if you can't do good CPR where they are. BC's endpoints: thirty minutes with no return of circulation and no shocks, or forty minutes if there was any return of circulation or any shock. And consult medical oversight to stop the arrest on scene.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有驾驶相关的流程，但有一条 BC 规定直接关系到转运。书上说，心脏骤停病人应走地面送最近的医院，而不是等直升机。BC 的心肺复苏指引补充：车辆静止时心肺复苏更有效。对儿童、低体温、创伤或可逆病因，可以边转运边做心肺复苏。只有现场危险，或病人所在位置无法有效按压时，才在复苏早期搬动病人。BC 的终止时间点：没有自主循环恢复、也没有电击过，满三十分钟；如果曾有自主循环恢复或电击过，满四十分钟。要在现场终止复苏，须咨询医疗监督。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Four Ss: start, steer, stop, stay running. Brake fade once = out of service
  2. Lights and siren only ask; the attendant decides by patient stability
  3. Park as a buffer; spotter to back up; helicopter: front or side, not the tail

Next: Chapter 50, Medical Incident Command
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: an ambulance must start, steer, stop, and stay running every time; any threat to those four, including a single episode of brake fade, takes it out of service. Two: lights and siren only ask for the right of way. Drive with due regard, and as the attendant, choose emergency mode based on the patient's stability, nothing else. Three: park to protect the scene and yourself, back up only with a spotter, and approach a helicopter from the front or side, never near the tail rotor. Next class: Chapter 50, medical incident command, when one call becomes dozens of patients. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you then.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，救护车每次都必须能启动、转向、停车、持续运转；四项中任何一项受威胁，包括哪怕一次刹车衰减，都要停用。二，警灯警笛只是请求路权；要以应有注意驾驶，作为后舱负责人，是否走紧急模式只看病人是否稳定。三，停车要保护现场也保护自己，倒车一定要有指挥员，接近直升机要从前方或侧面，远离尾旋翼。下节课是第五十章，医疗事故指挥：一个呼叫变成几十个病人时怎么办。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
